narrative.text: The Coca-Cola Company, a beverage company, manufactures and sells various nonalcoholic beverages in the United States and internationally. The company provides Trademark Coca-Cola, sparkling soft drinks and flavors; water, sports, coffee, and tea; juice, value-added dairy, and plant-based beverages; and emerging beverages. It also offers beverage concentrates and syrups, as well as fountain syrups to fountain retailers comprising restaurants and convenience stores. The company sells its products under the Coca-Cola, Diet Coke/Coca-Cola Light, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, caffeine free Diet Coke, Cherry Coke, Fanta, Sprite, Simply, Fanta Orange, Fanta Zero Orange, Fanta Zero Sugar, Fanta Apple, Sprite Zero Sugar, Simply Orange, Simply Apple, Simply Grapefruit, Fresca, Schweppes, Thums Up, Aquarius, Ayataka, BODYARMOR, Ciel, Costa, Crystal, Dasani, Fuze Tea, Georgia, glacéau smartwater, glacéau vitaminwater, Gold Peak, I LOHAS, Powerade, Topo Chico, Core Power, Del Valle, fairlife, innocent, Maaza, Minute Maid, Minute Maid Pulpy, Santa Clara, and dogadan brands. It operates through a network of independent bottling partners, distributors, wholesalers, and retailers, as well as through bottling and distribution operators. The Coca-Cola Company was founded in 1886 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

base.writtenAnchor: The base case takes the business as the latest filings describe it: FY2025 revenue 47,941m with operating income 13,762m, a 28.7% margin, and a trailing twelve months of 49,284m after a quarter ended 2026-04-03 that grew 12.1% on the year (H:revenue, H:margin, H:quarter). That recent momentum is treated as partly durable but not extrapolated: growth is set at 4.5%, above the 1.5% nine-year window CAGR but far below the 12.1% latest quarter and well inside the filed single-year range (H:revenue, H:quarter). Margin holds at 27.5%, between the FY2019-FY2021 band of about 27% and the FY2025 peak, on the view that the FY2024 dip reflected charges rather than the underlying mix (H:margin). Returns on new capital are set at 15%, inside the 13.6%-16.1% filed ROIC band (H:returns), fading by year 10 to 12% \u2014 the 9% rate plus a wide-moat credit the filed returns support. Net reinvestment of 1.8% of revenue sits just above the 1.4% filed median, reflecting the capex uptrend (H:capex), and share count is held flat.

bear.writtenAnchor: Coca-Cola's filed decade shows a top line that barely grew: 41.9bn in FY2016 against 47.9bn in FY2025, a 1.5% window CAGR, with outright declines in FY2017, FY2018 and FY2020 (H:revenue). The bear case assumes the recent step-up is mostly pricing that fades, volumes stay flat in developed markets, and currency and refranchising keep reported revenue growing about 2% a year. Margin gives back the FY2025 peak and settles near the FY2023-FY2024 zone, where impairment and legal charges pulled operating margin to 21.2% (H:margin). Net reinvestment runs above the filed median as capex continues its climb from 1,177m in FY2020 to 2,112m in FY2025 while D&A falls to 1,050m (H:capex), and each new dollar earns 10% \u2014 below the 9% discount rate plus moat credit, i.e. growth that barely pays for itself. Share count drifts up slightly with stock compensation of roughly 279m a year and no buyback disclosure in the supplied sources (H:cashflow).

bull.writtenAnchor: The bull case reads the quarter ended 2026-04-03 \u2014 revenue 12,472m, up 12.1%, trailing twelve months 49,284m \u2014 as the start of a faster stretch of pricing plus volume in developing markets, and holds revenue growth at 6.5% for five years, still well inside the filed single-year range that reached 17.1% (H:quarter, H:revenue). The refranchised, concentrate-heavy model is assumed to keep margin at 29.5%, roughly where FY2025's 28.7% landed and just above the top of the filed range (H:margin). Capital intensity stays light: net reinvestment of 1.4% of revenue, matching the filed median, as D&A of about 1.0bn offsets much of the 2.1bn capex (H:capex). New capital earns 19%, above the 16.1% best filed ROIC but inside the allowed 1.5x limit on the strength of a high-return, asset-light system (H:returns), fading to a 13.5% terminal return. Share count falls about 3% as cash flow comfortably covers stock compensation of roughly 279m (H:cashflow).

findings.evidence: Full-year operating cash flow of $7.4B sits well below full-year operating income of $13.8B, despite depreciation and amortisation of $1.1B and share-based compensation of $279.0M being non-cash add-backs that should push cash flow above accounting profit rather than below it. The record contains no reconciliation of the gap and no prior-year cash flow figures against which to judge whether it is recurring.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if the shortfall reflects a structural feature of the business (working capital, cash taxes, litigation or contingent-consideration settlements that recur) rather than a non-recurring outflow. A favourable case that leans on margin strength at 28.7% is leaning on a profit measure the cash statement in this same filing did not deliver.

findings.evidence: Cash FCF of $5.3B is derived from a single annual period: operating cash flow of $7.4B less capital expenditure of $2.1B. No multi-year FCF series was supplied for this company, so no base rate for conversion or volatility is available in this record and none can be constructed from it.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if the latest annual period is unrepresentative. With only a single observation in the record, a favourable case cannot demonstrate from these facts that the FCF level is normal rather than a trough or a peak.

findings.evidence: The debt figure of $43.8B is assembled from long-term debt and lease obligations plus the current portion plus commercial paper, and the source line states explicitly that short-term borrowings were not tagged at this period. Debt therefore reflects only the components that were tagged, and exceeds total equity of $33.6B by a wide margin before any untagged short-term element.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if untagged short-term borrowings are material. Any bridge from business value to equity value built on this figure inherits a known omission, and the omission runs in the direction that flatters equity holders.

findings.evidence: The label is cash and marketable debt securities, but the source line shows only cash and equivalents was tagged, with short-term investments not tagged at this period. The figure $10.6B is also identical to the standalone cash balance $10.6B, confirming no securities are included.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter wherever the cash figure is used as a deduction against debt. The understatement runs the opposite way to the debt understatement noted above, so the two do not reliably offset and the net position cannot be pinned down from this record.

findings.claimOrFactReference: Equity-method investments — disclosed quoted fair value (memo) (equity-method-investments-fair-value)
findings.evidence: Disclosed quoted fair value of equity-method investments is $34.3B, a sum of the same order as the entire reported total equity of $33.6B. These are unconsolidated holdings whose earnings contribution does not appear in operating income of $13.8B and whose value is marked by third-party quoted prices outside the company's control.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if a favourable case credits both the operating business and these stakes without separating them, or if it assumes the quoted value is stable. A material portion of the balance sheet is exposed to the market prices of other listed entities.

findings.evidence: Noncontrolling interests of $2.1B sit within the consolidated structure alongside total equity of $33.6B, meaning a portion of consolidated results and net assets does not accrue to the holders of the 4,302,482,418 shares shares outstanding.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if per-share reasoning is built off consolidated figures such as operating income of $13.8B or operating cash flow of $7.4B without first deducting the outside interest.

findings.evidence: Operating lease liabilities of $1.7B are carried as memo only and sit outside the debt figure of $43.8B. Alongside them the record carries unrecognized tax benefits of $857.0M and maximum guarantee exposure of $837.0M, both also memo and contingent.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if these obligations are claims ranking ahead of equity in substance. Treated as memo items they are invisible in the capital structure as filed, and together they are not trivial relative to the cash balance of $10.6B.

findings.evidence: Capital expenditure of $2.1B exceeds depreciation and amortisation of $1.1B for the same annual period, so the cash being put into fixed assets is running above the accounting charge taken against earnings.
findings.whatWouldHaveToBeTrue: This would matter if the excess is maintenance rather than growth spending. In that case reported operating income of $13.8B overstates what the asset base can distribute, and the record supplies no split between maintenance and growth capital and no prior-year capex against which to judge the trend.

statements.responsibility: GROWTH PATH AGAINST BASE RATES AND HISTORY
statements.statement: The supplied data gives margin history in depth but no revenue-growth base rate. Revenue appears only as the current-period figure $47.9B and the trailing twelve-month figure $49.3B; there is no filed distribution of annual growth rates in the catalogue. No base rate is available here against which the analyst's growth path can be checked, and I will not supply one from elsewhere. What the supplied figures do show is that the trailing twelve-month line sits above the latest filed-period line, which is consistent with the recent momentum the analyst's anchors describe but says nothing about its durability. For the base path to hold, the recent step-up would have to be partly structural rather than a pricing effect that laps out, with developed-market volumes at least stable and currency and refranchising not clawing reported revenue back. For the bull path to hold, the latest quarter's pace would have to mark the start of a sustained stretch of pricing plus developing-market volume rather than a single strong comparison. For the bear path to hold, the step-up would have to be almost entirely price, fading back toward the flat top line the analyst's anchor describes for the filed decade.

This model is fragile on this run, and the fragility is structural rather than marginal. The rate in use is 9.0% against a policy terminal growth rate of 3.0%, so the spread between them is wide enough that the terminal block does not explode mathematically — but the adopted fade structure is still a draft: Draft (assumption sheet version 1, not yet adopted): wide moat — the return on new capital fades to the rate by year 20 (bear by year 10); the terminal return is the rate (bull the rate + 1.5pp). The valuation is computed from the draft; the final verdict waits for adoption.. The checks that would normally measure fragility are not available. Revaluing the base case at a higher discount rate returns INCOMPLETE and at a lower rate INCOMPLETE, because no revalued base case was supplied for this run. The discount rate at which the base case equals today's price is INCOMPLETE, because enterprise value is itself INCOMPLETE and there is no per-share value to solve for. The fair-value range has been replaced by LEVERAGE UNSUPPORTED IN v1. With no rate-dependent output surviving, the model carries no valuation weight on this run; only the history and multiple diagnostics below are readable.

Most of the price-implied layer is unavailable. The reverse-DCF solve returns INCOMPLETE for the near-horizon growth the price demands, INCOMPLETE for the implied longer-run CAGR and INCOMPLETE for the implied revenue at the end of the projection, so the question of what growth the price embeds cannot be answered here. The steady-state enterprise value is LEVERAGE UNSUPPORTED IN v1, the present value of growth opportunities is LEVERAGE UNSUPPORTED IN v1 and its share of enterprise value is LEVERAGE UNSUPPORTED IN v1, so the split between what the business already earns and what it must still win is not readable. Enterprise value is INCOMPLETE, which in turn leaves EV/EBIT at INCOMPLETE and EV/EBITDA at INCOMPLETE. What survives is equity-level: at $93.42 as of 2026-10-19 the trailing earnings multiple is 28.1x and the free-cash-flow yield on market capitalisation is 1.3%, against cash free cash flow of $5.3B. Where that multiple sits in the company's own history is INCOMPLETE, and the supplied data contains no other multiple base rate, so no historical comparison can be made. The base scenario's implied exit multiple on final-year operating profit is 9.4x; the supplied data holds no base rate for exit multiples, so this figure stands uncompared.

The analyst's scenarios rest on the filed record where that record is thickest and on judgement where it is not. All of them lean on the operating-margin history, which the supplied data does carry: a current margin of 28.7% against a window median of 26.0%, a window range of 8.0% and a worst single-year change of 3.5% over a window of 10 years, drawn from 19 filed years. The capex and reinvestment settings are anchored to a described capex uptrend and a filed median, and the base case's return on new capital is placed inside a filed ROIC band. The least anchored parts are at the ends. The bull case sets margin above the top of the filed range and a return on new capital above the best filed year, justified by a limit rather than by observation, and assumes a falling share count that the supplied data does not evidence. The bear case pairs weak growth with reinvestment above the filed median and a return on new capital the anchor itself concedes barely covers the cost of that capital. All of this is moot for output purposes: the bear, base and bull values render as $NaN, $NaN and $NaN, the probability-weighted value as $NaN, and the price's location within the range is INCOMPLETE, because there is no debt-and-cash bridge to apply.

statements.responsibility: ASSUMPTION PLAUSIBILITY AND WHAT THE PRICE REQUIRES
statements.statement: On margin, the supplied history is the firmest ground available. The base case holds margin between the current level of 28.7% and the window median of 26.0%, which is inside the observed band; the window range of 8.0% shows that band is wide, and the worst single-year change of 3.5% shows moves within it have been gradual rather than violent. The bear margin sits below the median and the bull margin sits above the top of the filed range — the bull therefore asks for a margin the company has not posted in the window the data covers. On growth, no base rate exists in the supplied data, so the plausibility of any of the growth settings cannot be tested here. On returns, the implied return on new capital for the current fiscal year is INCOMPLETE, so the analyst's assumed returns cannot be checked against a computed current value. There is an internal tension in the bear case, which the anchor states openly: reinvestment is set above the filed median while new capital is assumed to earn roughly what it costs, so that growth consumes cash without adding value. The bull case carries the mirror tension, assuming both the lightest reinvestment and the highest return. As to what the price requires, the honest answer is that this run cannot state it: the reverse-DCF solve is INCOMPLETE and unlevered free cash flow is INCOMPLETE, with every rate-dependent output suppressed. What is observable is that at $93.42 the free-cash-flow yield is 1.3% against cash free cash flow of $5.3B, and the trailing earnings multiple is 28.1x — a price that is paid for future cash rather than for current cash return, with no computed figure here saying how much future cash.
